rounds.text: Iris Clothings Ltd is demonstrating exceptional operational momentum, evidenced by a 41% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months and a 36% compounded profit growth in the same period [E16, E19]. The company is effectively deploying capital, achieving an ROCE of 16.0% which significantly outperforms the sector benchmark of 8.39% [E10, E12]. This efficiency is further supported by the completion of major capital expenditure, as indicated by the 85.7% reduction in capital work in progress, signaling that new capacity is ready to drive future output [E35]. Institutional confidence is clearly building, with domestic institutions increasing their stake by 2.55% and overall positive money flow into the stock [E38, E39]. The company operates within a sector currently experiencing a positive tailwind, providing a supportive macro backdrop for its aggressive growth trajectory [E67, E69]. Conceded: the company faces challenges with negative operating and free cash flow as of March 2026 [E31, E32], and the current valuation metrics, including a P/E of 56.85x, sit well above sector benchmarks [E6, E11].

Iris Clothings Ltd currently trades at a significant valuation premium, with a P/E of 56.6x [E1] and a P/B of 5.78x, which dwarfs the sector benchmarks of 14.67x and 1.18x respectively [E6, E7]. This aggressive pricing is further highlighted by an EV/EBITDA of 32.94x compared to the sector’s 8.95x [E11], suggesting that the market has priced in perfection that the underlying financials struggle to justify. The company’s intrinsic value, calculated via DCF, sits at Rs 41 per share, implying a negative margin of safety of 35.5% at the current market price [E40, E41]. Furthermore, the business is currently burning cash, evidenced by negative operating and free cash flows of Rs -7 Cr and Rs -21 Cr respectively [E31, E32]. While the company has demonstrated historical growth, the promoter holding has declined by 12.15 percentage points since December 2023 [E36], and operating margins have compressed by 6 percentage points over the last three years [E26]. Conceded: the company has delivered strong compounded sales and profit growth [E14, E17] and maintains a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.30x [E33].

The bear’s focus on valuation multiples ignores that Iris Clothings is fundamentally outperforming its peers, justifying a premium through superior efficiency metrics like an ROE of 10.12% and ROCE of 11.95% compared to sector benchmarks of 7.18% and 8.39% [E9, E10]. While the bear cites high P/E and EV/EBITDA ratios [E1, E11], it fails to account for the company’s aggressive growth trajectory, with sales and profit compounding at 41% and 36% respectively in the trailing twelve months [E16, E19]. Conceded: the company is currently not paying a dividend [E4, E56], and the DCF model suggests a negative margin of safety [E40, E41]. Regarding cash flow, the negative figures in March 2026 [E31, E32] must be viewed alongside the fact that capital expenditure is largely completed, with CWIP down 85.7% as new capacity comes online [E35]. Although promoter holdings have decreased [E36], this has been met with positive institutional money flow and increased ownership by domestic institutions [E38, E39]. Finally, while operating margins have seen compression [E26], the company remains in a sector tailwind [E67, E69] and continues to deliver profit growth that significantly outpaces the sector [E17, E18, E70].

Conceded: the company demonstrates superior efficiency metrics with an ROE of 10.12% and ROCE of 11.95% against sector benchmarks [E9, E10], and sales and profit compound at 41% and 36% in the trailing twelve months [E16, E19]. However, pointing to these efficiency metrics ignores that the stock trades at an extreme P/E of 56.6x and EV/EBITDA of 32.94x, which massively outpace sector medians of 14.67x and 8.95x [E1, E6, E11]. Regarding capital expenditure, dismissing negative operating and free cash flows of Rs -7 Cr and Rs -21 Cr in March 2026 simply because CWIP declined by 85.7% [E32, E35] glosses over a severe cash conversion ratio of -0.44x and a warning that the company might be capitalizing interest costs [E30, E58]. Conceded: domestic institutions increased their ownership [E38, E39], but promoter holdings have dropped significantly by 12.15 percentage points since December 2023 [E36]. Finally, while the sector enjoys a tailwind [E67, E69], operating margins have compressed by 6 percentage points in the TTM period to 16% [E26], price growth has outpaced profit growth by 28% [E52], and a reverse DCF shows the current price demands an unrealistic 22.2% earnings growth [E42].

Conceded: the stock trades at elevated valuation multiples including a P/E of 56.6x and EV/EBITDA of 32.94x compared to sector benchmarks [E1, E6, E11], alongside compressed TTM operating margins and negative cash flows [E26, E32]. However, pointing to these valuation and cash metrics ignores that the company is backed by strong fundamental performance, including a high relative-strength rating of 100, 71.6% twelve-month price returns [E46, E47], and an 82 out of 100 rules-based screen score [E59]. Furthermore, while the bear highlights the drop in promoter holding [E36], it overlooks the fact that institutional money flow reads positive with domestic institutions increasing their stake to 2.55% [E38, E39]. Regarding the capital expenditure and interest capitalization warnings [E35, E58], the sharp 85.7% decline in CWIP demonstrates that capex is largely completed and new capacity is coming online [E35], positioning the business to leverage the strong textiles sector tailwind with a score of +0.59 [E69]. Conceded: the reverse DCF indicates the price implies a 22.2% earnings growth rate [E42], but this is supported by recent top-line momentum featuring compounded sales growth of 41% in the trailing twelve months and 19% over three years [E15, E16].

Conceded: compounded sales growth reached 41% in the trailing twelve months and 19% over three years [E15, E16], and domestic institutional ownership increased to 2.55% [E38, E39]. However, pointing to high relative strength and past price returns [E46, E47] offers no safety against a rich valuation where the price already discounts a 22.2% earnings growth rate, surpassing the base case of 18.0% [E42]. Furthermore, citing recent top-line momentum [E15, E16] ignores that operating margins have eroded by six percentage points to 16% in the TTM compared to three years earlier [E26], and quarterly margins remain inconsistent [E29]. Conceded: the textiles sector is in a tailwind with a score of +0.59 [E69] and the rules-based screen scored 82 out of 100 [E59]. Yet, dismissing the negative cash flows and capital expenditure warnings by pointing to declining CWIP [E35] overlooks the reality of negative free cash flow of Rs -21 Cr in Mar 2026 [E32], alongside potential interest capitalization [E58] and a significant drop in promoter holding of 12.15 percentage points since December 2023 [E36].
